t.6.102.1: Approaching Rāma, the greatly wise, the best of all bowmen, that monkey, who understood what was to the purpose, spoke these words.
t.6.102.2: You should see that queen Maithilī, tormented by grief, for whose sake this whole undertaking was begun and for whom these deeds have now borne their fruit.
t.6.102.3: For Maithilī, overwhelmed with grief, her eyes clouded with tears, was filled with joy on hearing of your victory.
t.6.102.5: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Rāma, the best of the upholders of dharma, suddenly fell into deep thought and was flooded with tears.
t.6.102.4: Trusting me because of her earlier confidence in me, she said to me: “I wish to see my husband, his purpose accomplished, together with Lakṣmaṇa.”
t.6.102.6: Heaving a long and hot sigh and gazing at the earth, he spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa, who stood before him, resembling a cloud.
t.6.102.7: Bring Sītā, the princess of Videha, here without delay, her head bathed, her limbs anointed with heavenly unguents, and adorned with heavenly ornaments.
t.6.102.8: Thus addressed by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa hastened and, entering the inner apartments, had Sītā summoned through his own women.
t.6.102.9: Vaidehī, anointed with divine unguents and adorned with divine ornaments, mount the palanquin, blessings be upon you; your husband wishes to see you.
t.6.102.10: Thus addressed, Vaidehī replied to Vibhīṣaṇa: "O lord of the rākṣasas, I wish to see my husband just as I am, without bathing."
t.6.102.11: Hearing those words of hers, Vibhīṣaṇa replied: “Just as I and Rāma, your husband, have directed, so you ought to do it.”
t.6.102.12: Hearing those words of his, the virtuous Maithilī, who revered her brother as a deity and was steadfast in her vow of devotion to her husband, replied, "So be it."
t.6.102.13: Then Sītā, her head freshly bathed, adorned by young women, decked with costly ornaments and wearing costly garments…
t.6.102.14: Having seated her in a shining palanquin covered with costly cloths and guarded by many rākṣasas, Vibhīṣaṇa brought her there.
t.6.102.15: Approaching the great-souled one and seeing that he was absorbed in deep thought, he bowed low and, filled with joy, announced that Sītā had arrived.
t.6.102.16: Upon hearing that she had come, she who had long dwelt in the house of the rākṣasa, three feelings at once, joy, dejection and anger, entered Rāghava.
t.6.102.17: Then, seeing Vibhīṣaṇa standing at his side, Rāghava, joyless and pondering with deliberation, spoke these words to him.
t.6.102.18: O lord of the Rākṣasas, gentle one, ever devoted to my victory, let Vaidehī come quickly into my presence.
t.6.102.19: Having understood that command of Rāghava, Vibhīṣaṇa swiftly had efforts made on every side to clear the crowd away.
t.6.102.20: There, men wearing jackets and turbans, holding canes and drums in their hands, moved about on all sides, driving the crowds back.
t.6.102.21: Then, on every side, they drove far away the crowds of bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas that were being pushed back.
t.6.102.22: As they were all being driven back, a clamor rose up from them, like the roar of the ocean surging up under the wind.
t.6.102.23: Seeing them being driven back, thrown into confusion on every side, Rāghava, out of kindness and out of indignation at that treatment, put a stop to it.
t.6.102.24: And Rāma, enraged, as if burning him with his eyes, spoke these reproachful words to the greatly wise Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.102.25: Why, disregarding me, are these people being harassed by you? Stop this effort; these people are my own people.
t.6.102.26: Neither houses nor garments nor walls nor screens, nor such royal honours as these, are a woman's covering; her conduct is her veil.
t.6.102.28: This woman has come into the midst of war and stands in great distress; there can be no fault in her being seen, especially in my presence.
t.6.102.27: In times of calamity and hardship, in war, at a svayaṃvara, at a sacrifice, or at a wedding, the seeing of women is not held to be improper.
t.6.102.29: Therefore, O Vibhīṣaṇa, bring her quickly near me. Let this Sītā see me standing here, surrounded by my host of friends.
t.6.102.30: Thus addressed by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa, full of misgiving, humbly brought Sītā into Rāma's presence.
t.6.102.31: Then Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, and Hanūmān the monkey, having heard the words of Rāma, became deeply distressed.
t.6.102.32: And from his harsh gestures, indifferent to his wife, they surmised that Rāghava was, as it were, displeased with Sītā.
t.6.102.33: But Maithilī, shrinking into her own limbs out of modesty, approached her husband, followed by Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.102.34: She, her face covered with her garment out of modesty in the assembly of people, reached her husband and wept, saying only, "Āryaputra!"
t.6.102.35: Out of wonder, out of joy and out of love, weeping, she whose face was gentler still gazed upon the gentle face of her husband.
t.6.102.36: Then, gazing upon the face of her beloved, long unseen, lovely as the full moon newly risen, she cast off the weariness of her mind, and her own face then became like the spotless moon.
